year3.title: The Curious Little Otter
year3.imagePrompt: a curious playful otter exploring a sparkling river with smooth pebbles and lily pads, children's watercolour, magical woodland scene
lines: Oliver the otter lived beside a sparkling river.
Every morning he would explore the smooth river stones.
One day he discovered a shiny silver key underwater.
He wondered what amazing treasure the key might unlock.
His clever friend, a wise old turtle, had an idea.
Together they followed the river until they reached a cave.
Inside the cave was a small wooden chest covered in moss.
The key fit perfectly and the chest opened with a creak.
It was full of beautiful coloured pebbles collected long ago.
Oliver and the turtle laughed and shared the treasure with everyone.

year3.title: Bramble the Brave Badger
year3.imagePrompt: a brave little badger wearing a small red scarf walking through an enchanted forest at twilight, fireflies glowing, children's watercolour illustration
lines: Bramble the badger was the smallest animal in the forest.
The other creatures often teased him because of his tiny size.
One evening a terrible storm shook the trees and scattered the birds.
A baby squirrel became trapped beneath a heavy fallen branch.
Bramble was the only one brave enough to crawl underneath.
He pushed with all his strength and freed the frightened squirrel.
The animals of the forest cheered loudly for their tiny hero.
From that day on nobody ever teased Bramble about his size.
They learned that courage has nothing to do with being big.

year3.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Cat
year3.imagePrompt: a striped tabby cat sitting in a lighthouse window on a stormy night, warm glowing light, dramatic crashing waves, children's watercolour illustration
lines: High on the rocky cliffs stood a tall striped lighthouse.
Inside lived Cornelius the lighthouse keeper and his clever cat Pip.
Every night Pip would climb to the very top of the lighthouse.
She watched the dark ocean carefully for any ships in danger.
One stormy Tuesday the lighthouse lamp flickered and went out completely.
Pip raced down the spiral staircase and woke Cornelius immediately.
Together they replaced the broken bulb before any ship could crash.
The grateful sailors sent a beautiful painting of their ship as a gift.
Cornelius hung it proudly on the lighthouse wall for everyone to see.
And Pip purred loudly every time she walked past her favourite painting.

year3.title: The Inventor's Workshop
year3.imagePrompt: a clever fox in goggles and overalls surrounded by whimsical inventions and colourful gadgets in a busy workshop, children's watercolour illustration
lines: Professor Fennec the fox had the most incredible workshop in the valley.
Every shelf was crowded with inventions, experiments, and unfinished contraptions.
His greatest challenge was building a machine that could translate animal languages.
He worked tirelessly through the night, surrounded by gears and glowing dials.
One morning the machine spluttered, hummed, and suddenly crackled to life.
He pointed it at a passing sparrow and heard her beautiful song translated.
She was singing about her favourite berry bush and the colour of the sky.
Professor Fennec laughed with delight and ran outside to speak with everyone.
The entire forest gathered to share their stories, worries, and wonderful dreams.
From that day on the valley was the most peaceful, joyful place imaginable.

year3.title: Stargazing with Stella
year3.imagePrompt: a little owl with a brass telescope looking at a brilliant star-filled night sky from a hilltop, magical glowing stars, children's watercolour illustration
lines: Stella the owl had a magnificent brass telescope she had built herself.
Each cloudless night she would carry it to the top of Pinecone Hill.
She mapped every constellation and gave each one a wonderful new name.
Her favourite was the group of stars she called the Swimming Octopus.
One night she spotted something she had never seen in all her years.
A small bright object was crossing the sky in a perfectly straight line.
She recorded its position carefully in her battered leather notebook.
The next morning she sent a letter to the Royal Animal Observatory.
Three weeks later they wrote back confirming her extraordinary discovery.
Stella the owl had found a brand new comet, and they named it after her.

year3.title: The Dragon Who Loved Snow
year3.imagePrompt: a small purple dragon looking at a tiny snowflake with wonder, cosy cave home with cushions and books, children's watercolour illustration, magical
lines: Ember was the most unusual dragon in the entire Silverstone Mountains.
While all the other dragons breathed roaring flames with great pride, Ember could not.
The truth was that Ember could breathe the most spectacular glittering snowflakes.
In the deepest summer heat, animals would travel for miles to cool down nearby.
Ember decorated the whole mountain with sparkling frost patterns every single morning.
When the visiting queen arrived during a heatwave, Ember saved the royal celebration.
Her snowflakes swirled around the guests like a magical shimmering blizzard of light.
The other dragons shook their heads in disbelief and then began to cheer.
Nobody thought Ember was unusual at all after that remarkable summer day.
She was simply the most extraordinary dragon the mountains had ever known.

year3.title: The Clockmaker's Apprentice
year3.imagePrompt: a young hedgehog apprentice working on a large ornate clock with tiny gears and tools, golden workshop light, children's watercolour illustration
lines: Hazel the hedgehog was apprenticed to the great clockmaker Otto the beaver.
Every morning she polished the brass gears and carefully wound every single clock.
Otto taught her that patience was the most important tool in any workshop.
One afternoon a mysterious customer brought in a clock unlike anything they had seen.
Its face showed not the time but the weather, the tides, and the phases of the moon.
Hazel studied it for three whole weeks, sketching every part in her notebook.
She discovered a hidden compartment containing a tiny rolled-up musical scroll.
When the scroll was placed inside the clock, it played a beautiful ancient melody.
The mysterious customer returned, listened quietly, and wept with joyful tears.
It had belonged to his grandmother, and the song was her favourite lullaby.

year3.title: The Lost Map
year3.imagePrompt: two young animal adventurers holding a treasure map on a tropical island with palm trees and bright flowers, children's watercolour illustration
lines: Captain Thistle the rabbit had sailed every ocean in her tiny striped vessel.
Her first mate, a philosophical tortoise named Gerard, kept the ship's log.
One foggy morning they discovered an old rolled map tucked inside a bottle.
The map showed a mysterious island shaped exactly like a slice of melon.
They followed the map for eleven days through storms and glassy-calm waters.
When they finally arrived the island was covered in enormous sweetly scented flowers.
Every flower contained a small note written by the explorer who came before them.
The notes described extraordinary creatures that could only be seen at midnight.
Captain Thistle and Gerard stayed for a whole month filling notebook after notebook.
They sailed home with stories so remarkable that nobody believed a single word.

year3.title: The Orchestra Underground
year3.imagePrompt: a magical underground cavern filled with glowing mushrooms and animal musicians playing instruments, children's watercolour illustration, magical and warm
lines: Beneath the roots of the oldest tree in Fernwood lived an extraordinary orchestra.
The musicians were moles, voles, beetles, and one exceptionally gifted earthworm.
They played every night for the sleeping roots, who seemed to grow more beautifully because of it.
Their conductor was Maestro Deepburrow, a mole with silver spectacles and a long baton.
One spring evening a young fox cub named Rufus fell through a mossy trapdoor.
He landed softly in the front row just as the orchestra began their finest symphony.
Rufus sat perfectly still, barely breathing, not wanting the music to ever stop.
When it ended, Maestro Deepburrow invited him to join as the triangle player.
Rufus practised every night until his triangle rang out clear and perfectly in tune.
And the roots of the old tree grew taller and stronger than they ever had before.

year3.title: The Painter of Skies
year3.imagePrompt: a magical pelican with rainbow-tipped wings painting a spectacular sunset sky with a giant brush, children's watercolour illustration, breathtaking colours
lines: High above the clouds lived a pelican whose wings were tipped with every colour imaginable.
Her name was Iris, and she had the most important job in the entire world.
Every morning before sunrise she would pick up her enormous feather brush.
She swept it carefully across the horizon to paint the colours of the dawn.
Every evening she mixed purples, golds, and crimsons for the magnificent sunset.
One winter morning she woke with a dreadful cold and could not paint at all.
The sky stayed a flat dull grey for the whole of that unhappy Tuesday.
Every animal looked up sadly, knowing something wonderful was missing from their day.
Her friend, a determined starling named Cleo, painted in her place that evening.
Iris looked down at the crooked wobbling colours and laughed until she felt much better.
